script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

A cozy apartment. The aroma of burnt popcorn wafts through the air. SARAH (30s, a high-strung, tech-savvy woman) sits cross-legged on the couch, her gaze fixed on her computer screen. Her roommate, MARK (early 30s, a laid-back artist) enters, carrying a bowl of freshly popped popcorn.

MARK
(cheerfully)
Movie night, huh? What's the pick?

SARAH
(frustrated)
The usual. Document number 237. It's due tomorrow.

MARK
(sympathetically)
Long night ahead, huh? I'll leave you to it.

SARAH
(sighs)
Thanks.

MARK
(smiling)
You're welcome.

MARK exits, leaving SARAH to her work.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

The next morning, SARAH sits at a table, sipping a coffee and scrolling through her emails. She receives a notification - a new message from her ex-boyfriend, JACK (early 30s, a stubborn, egotistical man).

SARAH
(annoyed)
What could he want now?

She opens the email, her face contorting into a look of shock and anger as she reads the contents.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

SARAH storms into the living room, her eyes red from crying. Mark looks up from his painting, alarmed.

SARAH
(angrily)
He's back! He's trying to ruin my life again!

MARK
(concerned)
What did he do?

SARAH
(tearfully)
He published that article. The one I wrote for him. He changed it. He made me look foolish!

MARK
(sympathetically)
Oh, no. That's terrible.

SARAH
(desperately)
I need to do something. I can't let him get away with this.

MARK
(calmly)
Maybe you should try talking to him.

SARAH
(scoffing)
Talking to him? He doesn't even deserve that.

MARK
(firmly)
Sarah, you can't let your anger control you. You need to forgive him. It's the only way you can move on.

INT. APARTMENT BUILDING LOBBY - DAY

SARAH stands outside Jack's apartment, her heart pounding in her chest. She takes a deep breath, then knocks on the door.

JACK opens the door, looking surprised to see her.

SARAH
(sternly)
I came to talk.

JACK
(surprised)
You did? I thought you'd be furious.

SARAH
(frankly)
I am, but I also realize something. I can't let my anger consume me. I forgive you for what you did.

Jack looks taken aback, unsure of how to react.

JACK
(tentatively)
I'm sorry. I didn't mean to hurt you.

SARAH
(softly)
I know you didn't. But you did. And I forgive you.

They stand there, looking at each other, the weight of their past mistakes dissolving between them.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Sarah sits on the couch, her laptop open in front of her. She smiles as she reads the positive responses to an article she's written - one that she's proud of, free from Jack's interference.

Mark enters, looking at her with admiration.

MARK
(proudly)
You did it.

SARAH
(smiling)
I did.

MARK
(grinning)
I knew you could.

SARAH
(laughing)
You always believe in me.

MARK
(smiling)
That's what friends are for.

They share a laugh, their bond stronger than ever.

FADE OUT.
